title: Lifting a finite free quotient to a monoid product
statement:
Let $P,Q$ be integral commutative monoids, written additively, and let $q:P\to Q$ be a surjective monoid homomorphism. Here integrality means injectivity of the canonical maps into the group completions $G=P^{\rm gp}$ and $H=Q^{\rm gp}$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]; identify $P\subseteq G$ and $Q\subseteq H$. Let $U=P^\times=\{u\in P:-u\in P\}$ be its subgroup of units [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Suppose the induced group homomorphism $\pi:G\to H$ is surjective with $\ker\pi=U$. Suppose $H$ has a finite $\mathbf Z$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$, meaning that every element has a unique expression $\sum_i n_i e_i$, $n_i\in\mathbf Z$; $r=0$ is allowed. Then there is a group homomorphism $t:H\to G$ with $\pi t=1_H$ and $t(Q)\subseteq P$. Its restriction $j:Q\to P$ is a monoid homomorphism with $qj=1_Q$. The maps
$$F:Q\oplus U\longrightarrow P,\quad F(b,u)=j(b)+u,\qquad E:P\longrightarrow Q\oplus U,\quad E(p)=(q(p),p-j(q(p)))$$
are well-defined inverse monoid isomorphisms, and $q(F(b,u))=b$. Here $Q\oplus U$ is the Cartesian product with componentwise addition, and the second coordinate of $E$ is computed in $G$.

source.place: VI 3.7(a), printed p.75 (splitting the group sequence and restricting a section); VIII 3.1.11 and 3.1.26, printed pp.100,102 (local lift comparison). Agent algebraic refinement, extracting old steps 3--5, not a verbatim theorem of ILO.

proof.text: Using the group completions of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], regard $P\subseteq G$ and $Q\subseteq H$ as in the hypotheses. For each basis vector $e_i$, choose $g_i\in G$ with $\pi(g_i)=e_i$, possible by surjectivity of $\pi$. Define $t(\sum_i n_i e_i)=\sum_i n_i g_i$. Unique basis coordinates make this well-defined; coordinates of a sum are the sums of the coordinates, so $t$ is additive and $t(0)=0$. Moreover $\pi t(\sum_i n_i e_i)=\sum_i n_i e_i$, so $\pi t=1_H$. Empty sums give the same construction when $r=0$.

source.place: VI 3.7(a), printed p.75: splitting the abelian-group sequence and restricting the section to Q; explicit elementary algebraic refinement by Q119.

proof.text: For $b\in Q$, choose $p\in P$ with $q(p)=b$, using surjectivity of $q$. Since $\pi|_P=q$, one has $\pi(t(b)-p)=b-b=0$, hence $u=t(b)-p\in\ker\pi=U$. The unit definition in [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup] gives $u,-u\in P$, so $t(b)=p+u\in P$. Thus $j=t|_Q$ takes values in $P$. In $G$ we have $j(b+b^{\prime})=t(b+b^{\prime})=t(b)+t(b^{\prime})=j(b)+j(b^{\prime})$ and $j(0)=t(0)=0$; injectivity of $P\to G$ makes these equalities hold in $P$. Also $qj(b)=\pi t(b)=b$ in $H$, hence in $Q$ by injectivity of $Q\to H$.

source.place: VI 3.7(a), printed p.75: splitting the abelian-group sequence and restricting the section to Q; explicit elementary algebraic refinement by Q119.

proof.text: For $p\in P$, set $d(p)=p-j(q(p))\in G$. Then $\pi(d(p))=q(p)-qj(q(p))=0$, so $d(p)\in U$ by the assumed kernel equality. Thus $E(p)=(q(p),d(p))$ is well-defined. For $p,p^{\prime}\in P$, additivity of $q$ and $j$ gives $d(p+p^{\prime})=p+p^{\prime}-j(q(p)+q(p^{\prime}))=p+p^{\prime}-j(q(p))-j(q(p^{\prime}))=d(p)+d(p^{\prime})$ by commutativity in $G$, and $d(0)=0-j(0)=0$. Hence $E$ preserves addition and zero, with the subgroup operations on $U$ specified in the hypotheses.

source.place: VI 3.7(a), printed p.75: splitting the abelian-group sequence and restricting the section to Q; explicit elementary algebraic refinement by Q119.

proof.text: For $b\in Q,u\in U$, both $j(b)$ and $u$ lie in $P$, so $F(b,u)=j(b)+u\in P$. In $P$, additivity of $j$ and commutativity give $F((b,u)+(b^{\prime},u^{\prime}))=j(b+b^{\prime})+u+u^{\prime}=j(b)+u+j(b^{\prime})+u^{\prime}=F(b,u)+F(b^{\prime},u^{\prime})$ and $F(0,0)=0$. Since $u\in\ker\pi$, $q(u)=0$ in $H$ and hence in $Q$ by integrality of $Q$. Therefore $q(F(b,u))=qj(b)+q(u)=b$.

source.place: VI 3.7(a), printed p.75: splitting the abelian-group sequence and restricting the section to Q; explicit elementary algebraic refinement by Q119.

proof.text: For $p\in P$, compute $F(E(p))=j(q(p))+p-j(q(p))=p$ in $G$, hence in $P$ by integrality. For $(b,u)\in Q\oplus U$, Step 4 gives $q(F(b,u))=b$, so $E(F(b,u))=(b,j(b)+u-j(b))=(b,u)$: the second-coordinate equality holds in $G$ and hence in its subgroup $U$. Thus $FE=1_P$ and $EF=1_{Q\oplus U}$. Together with Steps 3--4 this proves the asserted inverse monoid isomorphisms and the projection identity.
